title: What stays when four positive tokens leave five?
description: Five positive tokens sit on a tray and four of them are taken away. The token that stays is positive. Keeko thinks the minus sign makes the answer negative.
teaching_notes: One idea: subtraction with tokens is taking tokens away, and the tokens that stay keep their own colour. Watch for students who let the minus sign decide the sign of the answer.

source: Example: Let us subtract (+5) - (+4). From 5 positives take away 4 positives to see the result.
video_script.why: The child subtracts positive tokens from positive tokens by taking them away and reads the sign from the tokens that stay.
video_script.substitution: Lift the tokens being subtracted off the tray and read the answer from the tokens that stay.
video_script.wrong_move: lets the minus sign in the question make the answer negative, instead of looking at the colour of the token that stays
video_script.payoff_line: Positive five take away positive four leaves positive one.
maths_rules: (+5) means 5 positive tokens; (+4) means 4 positive tokens
subtraction here is take away: from 5 positive tokens take away 4 positive tokens
slip: the minus sign says take away; it does not make the tokens that stay negative
video_script.design: One idea: take the tokens away and read the answer from the tokens that stay. Positive tokens are green as in the book. Keeko's doubt is that the minus sign makes the answer negative.
